newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM SEES NO NEED TO UP AIR FREIGHT USAGE.
newsitem.headline: GM SEES NO NEED TO UP AIR FREIGHT USAGE.

text.p: U.S. automaker General Motors Corp said on Tuesday it had no plans to increase its use of air freight to support its globalisation of car production.
"I don't think air freight will play a significant or increasing role for us," GM Europe President Richard Donnelly told Reuters. "It's expensive -- the train and the truck are the best way."
GM also prefers to avoid delivering parts to its assembly plants over distances that often require air freight, including shipments over oceans, Donnelly added.
"Our policy is to produce and purchase parts in each of the regions where we assemble cars," he said.
Donnelly was in Hungary for two days of talks with government officials about ways to increase cooperation with the country's auto parts industry.
